argument: The cut must be felt as a dry passage in the stroke's rerouting, not merely seen as a rust-coloured scar laid over a stable field.
The dark channel should make the wet mark visibly leave and re-enter its lane; a caption-free comparison must identify the same bend before and after lifting.
Opening a cut by pointer or keyboard must rebuild later stroke geometry, and lifting the latest cut must restore the exact preceding memory state.
Dry traces are an easy signal. Hold the candidate unless the rerouted mark carries the consequence when channel witnesses are ignored.
